study_identification.author_journal_year: Wu and Baeken, Biological Psychiatry: Global Open Science, 2024
study_identification.title: Sex Determines Anterior Cingulate Cortex Cortical Thickness in the Course of Depression

study_characteristics.study_objective: To examine whether sex differences affect anterior cingulate cortex (ACC) cortical thickness and its subregions differently during the course of depressive illness (first-episode versus recurrent major depressive disorder), using linear mixed-effects models and normative modeling.

dataset_name.supporting_text: Structural brain imaging data were used from the REST-MetaMDD Consortium (35), which consists of 25 research groups in 17 hospitals in China. Together, the consortium included 2428 collected datasets (1300 currently depressed individuals and 1128 healthy control participants [HCs]; age range, 12-82 years)... Consequently, 499 patients with MDD (381 first-episode MDD, 118 recurrent MDD) and 524 HCs with an age range of 12 to 77 years were selected from 9 study sites.

preprocessing_pipeline.answer: SPM12; ANTs DiReCT; DARTEL; HCP multimodal parcellation atlas
preprocessing_pipeline.reason: The Imaging Data section provides detailed description of the preprocessing pipeline including specific software and algorithms used.
preprocessing_pipeline.supporting_text: The anatomical images were first biasfield corrected and segmented into gray matter, white matter, and cerebrospinal fluid using the SPM12 (http://www.fil.ion.ucl.ac.uk/spm) toolbox. Then, CT estimation was further performed by the DiReCT (diffeomorphic registration-based cortical thickness) algorithm available in ANTs (Advanced Normalization Tools) (38). As suggested by Schwarz et al. (39), SPM12 segmentation input to ANTs thickness (SPM+DiReCT) method was the most reliable of all the thickness-based measures. Finally, the resulting CT maps were modulated and resampled into 2x2x2 mm using the DARTEL (Diffeomorphic Anatomical Registration using Exponentiated Lie algebra) algorithm (40).

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: Linear mixed-effects models (AFNI 3dLMEr) testing main effects of group and Group×Sex interactions on ACC CT with covariates (age, sex, education) and site-specific random effects. Post hoc simple effects tests with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction. Separate analyses for entire ACC and subdivisions (dACC, pgACC, sgACC) and for left/right hemispheres. LME models also tested relationships between HAMD scores and ACC CT within first-episode and recurrent MDD groups separately, with age, sex, education, and medication as covariates. Sensitivity analyses conducted with matched groups, including/excluding adolescents, including patients with unknown medication status, and restricting to HAMD>17.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: Sex determines ACC cortical thickness changes over the course of depressive illness: females showed thinner ACC CT overall; female first-episode MDD patients showed significantly thinner ACC CT (especially pgACC and sgACC) compared to male first-episode patients; male first-episode MDD patients showed thicker ACC CT compared to both male recurrent MDD patients and healthy males.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: Overall, females displayed significantly thinner ACC CT compared with males regardless of depression status. Female patients with first-episode MDD showed significantly thinner ACC CT compared with male first-episode MDD patients (Cohen's d = -0.65), including in the perigenual ACC and subgenual ACC, but not in the dorsal ACC. Male patients with first-episode depression showed thicker ACC CT (including subgenual ACC and pregenual ACC) compared to male patients with recurrent MDD (Cohen's d = 1.24), and also showed significantly thicker cortices in the same subregions compared to never-depressed males (Cohen's d = 0.85). No lateralization differences were observed in ACC CT or its subdivisions. The findings were consistent when analyzed using normative model z-scores (Figures S3-S5). The LME model showed no relationship between HAMD scores and CT in the ACC or its subdivisions in either first-episode or recurrent MDD groups. Results remained consistent across sensitivity analyses including matched groups for medication, exclusion of adolescents, inclusion of patients with unknown medication status, and restriction to moderate-to-severe depression (HAMD>17).
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: Cross-sectional design (not longitudinal follow-up of same patients); all recruitment sites in Asia (China), limiting generalizability; unavailability of information on number of episodes, duration of treatment, age at first episode (for recurrent group), or early adverse events; imbalance in group sizes (381 first-episode vs 118 recurrent MDD); inability to distinguish depression subtypes (e.g., melancholic, anxious) or identify treatment-resistant cases; focus limited to ACC (other brain areas/networks not examined); lack of sex-specific physiological variables (hormones, etc.); small but significant age difference between sexes; lack of formal independent validation of normative models.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: Authors suggest that sex-specific (psycho)therapeutic interventions targeting dysfunctional emotion regulation processes should be initiated early during the first depressive episode. Noninvasive brain stimulation methods such as repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation affecting sgACC processes may be of interest when patients do not reach full remission or are treatment-resistant. The normative modeling approach was used as an additional validation method, with similar findings observed for both raw CT values and z-scores derived from the normative model.

general_notes.general_notes: The paper was published online in 2023 (DOI: 10.1016/j.bpsgos.2023.08.003) in Biological Psychiatry: Global Open Science. The full REST-Meta-MDD Consortium dataset included 2428 participants (1300 MDD, 1128 HC) from 25 research groups across 17 hospitals, but the current study used a subset of 1023 participants (499 MDD, 524 HC) from 9 sites after applying quality control and exclusion criteria. The study is part of the REST-meta-MDD Project from DIRECT Consortium (http://doi.org/10.57760/sciencedb.o00115.00013). The Key Resources Table in supplementary materials lists software versions: MATLAB v9.9, AFNI 20210206, SPM12 r7771, ANTs, R 4.2.3, and R package lmerTest. The imaging pipeline combined SPM12 segmentation with ANTs DiReCT thickness estimation (described as most reliable by Schwarz et al. 2016), followed by DARTEL resampling. Site effects were handled through model-based approaches (random effects in LME and HBR) rather than batch-removal methods like ComBat. The normative modeling was performed using PCNToolkit v0.18 with hierarchical Bayesian regression, but no model performance metrics (EV, MSLL, skewness, kurtosis) were reported. The study found medication status did not affect ACC CT results based on additional linear mixed model analyses including medication as a factor.
